questions.question: Mention the prenatal diagnostic techniques.
questions.solution_html:
• Mention the prenatal diagnostic techniques.
  • Ultrasonography, Amniocentesis, Chorionic Villus Sampling, Maternal Blood Tests(two points with 1
  • mark each).
  • Enhance the educational experiences. Support children's development across various domains.
  • Make learning engaging and effective. (two points with (1 mark) each).
  • Nutritional needs: Due to the growth spurt and hormonal changes, adolescents require increased
  • energy and nutrients.Balanced nutrition is vital for maintaining physical health, hormonal balance
  • and mental alertness.
  • Key Nutritional Needs
  • • Energy-rich foods: needed for rapid growth and daily activity.
  • • Proteins: For muscle and tissue development.
  • • Calcium and Vitamin D: For bone and teeth formation.
  • • Iron: Especially important for girls to prevent anemia after menstruation begins.
  • • Vitamins and Minerals: Strengthen immunity and metabolism.
  • • Water: Maintains hydration and helps body functions.((5 marks))
questions.final_answer: Option (d) For bone and teeth formation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Identify any two factors that influence the development of foetus.
questions.solution_html:
• Maternal malnutrition, Drugs, Rh factor, Infectious disease of the mother, Age of mother
  • Emotional condition of mother, X-ray and radiation, Uterine crowding, Maternal attitude(two
  • points with (1 mark) each).
  • Structural Abnormalities:Involve changes in chromosome structure.Eg:a) Deletions: A portion
  • of the chromosome will be missing.b)Duplications: A portion of the chromosome is present in
  • excess. c)Translocations:A segment of one chromosome breaks off and attaches to another
  • chromosome.d)Inversions: A segment of the chromosome is flipped and rejoined, so the order of
  • genes is reversed.e)Insertion:A segment of one chromosome is inserted into another chromosome.
  • Lifestyle Needs: A balanced lifestyle helps build discipline, resilience, and emotional maturity
  • essential for adulthood.
  • Key Lifestyle Needs
  • • Regular Physical Activity improves fitness, confidence, and mood.
  • • Adequate sleepsupports brain development and emotional regulation.
  • • Personal Hygieneprevent infections and maintain self-esteem.
  • • Screen Time Management or Limited use of phones and gadgets helps to prevent eye strain
  • and sleep problems.
  • • Avoiding Risk Behaviors: Say no to smoking, alcohol, drugs, and unhealthy peer
  • influence.((5 marks))
questions.final_answer: Option Deletions: A portion
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: State the main function of the placenta.
questions.solution_html:
• Supplies nutrients and oxygen to the embryo.Removes waste products and carbon dioxide from the
  • embryo’s blood(two points with (1 mark) each).

  • Inherited genetic mutations((2 marks)).Effects:May result in birth defects, intellectual disabilities, or

questions.question: Discuss the common emotional and behaviour problems in adolescence.
questions.solution_html:

  • feeling of guilt, fear, worry, anxiety, jealousy, depression, hostility etc. due to physical changes

questions.question: Outline the objectives of Baby-Friendly Hospitals Initiative.
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the objectives of Baby-Friendly Hospitals Initiative.
  • To protect, promote, and support breastfeeding.To ensure early initiation and successful
  • continuation of breastfeeding.To encourage hospitals to provide optimal care for mothers and
  • infants.To strengthen mother–baby bonding through rooming-in and supportive practices.To train
  • healthcare staff to guide and assist mothers in breastfeeding(five points with (1 mark) each).

questions.question: Compare occupational therapy and behavioural therapy in helping children through early intervention.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare occupational therapy and behavioural therapy in helping children through early
  • intervention.
  • Occupational Therapy aims to enhance a child’s ability to perform daily living activities and also
  • supports sensory integration, hand–eye coordination, and independence in school and home
  • routines((2.5 marks)).Behavioural Therapy addresses emotional, behavioural, and social issues and
  • helps in developing self-control, positive social interactions, and coping strategies((2.5 marks)).
questions.final_answer: helps in developing self-control, positive social interactions, and coping strategies()
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Identify the major adjustments a neonate has to make immediately after birth.
questions.solution_html:
• ANeonate can be defined as a new born baby in the first 2 weeks after birth((1 mark) for
  • definition).Adjustment to temperature changes, Adjustment to breathing, Adjustment to sucking
  • and swallowing, Adjustment to elimination((1 mark) for explaining each four points).
questions.final_answer: and swallowing, Adjustment to elimination( for explaining each four points)

questions.question: Explain the importance of school readiness in early childhood education.
questions.solution_html:
• School Readiness is the stage at which a child is prepared to successfully enter and adapt to formal
  • schooling, both academically and socially((1 mark) for definition).
  • Importance:Smooth Transition: children can adapt to the school environment, leading to a more
  • successful educational experience. Long-Term Success:Children are more likely to perform well
  • academically and develop positive attitudes toward school(2 marksfor eachtwo points).
questions.final_answer: academically and develop positive attitudes toward school(2 marksfor eachtwo points)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse the effects of permissive technique of developing discipline among children.
questions.solution_html:

  • In permissive technique, no limits or boundaries are set for the child by the parent&too much
  • leniency and freedom for children((1 mark) for characteristics).Effects: The child become confused
  • insecure, and anxious, Lack clear sense of right and wrong, Show aggressiveness and resentment
  • Turn unmanageable at home, school, or neighborhood, Expect too much tolerance from other(1
  • mark each for any four points).
questions.final_answer: mark each for any four points)

questions.question: Analyse the role of play in child development.
questions.solution_html:

  • cultural understandings. Helps children express their thoughts and feelings, Develop language and
  • literacy skills and concepts.Provides opportunities to meet and solve problems((1 mark) each for any
  • four points).

questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the common causes of conflict between parents and adolescents.
  • Independence demanded by adolescents. Differences in opinions, values, and

questions.question: Describe types, causes and effects of chromosomal abnormalities.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction:Chromosomal abnormalities are changes in the number or structure of chromosomes
  • that can lead to developmental issues, genetic disorders, or diseases.((1 mark))
  • Types: 1) Numerical Abnormalities:Involve a change in chromosome number. Eg: a)Down
  • syndrome- (Trisomy 21-An extra copy of chromosome 21 for a total of 47 chromosomes. b) Turner
  • Syndrome- Monosomy X. It is a genetic condition that affects females, resulting from a missing or
  • altered X chromosome((2.5 marks)).
questions.final_answer: Option Down
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the meaning, need and importance of early stimulation and early intervention.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction & Meaning: Early Stimulation means the set of activities and experiences provided
  • from birth to encourage the child’s sensory, motor, cognitive, language, and social
  • development.Early Intervention means the planned services and supports given to infants and
  • young children with developmental delays or disabilities, to improve their overall growth and
  • functioning((4 marks)- 2 each).
  • Need and importance: Supports brain development.Prevents delays in development. Helps to
  • identify developmental problems early and prevents further complications.Provides special support
  • guidance, and therapies to maximize the child’s potential.Strengthens parent–child bonding. Helps
  • children become independent and live a better life.((6 marks) – for 6 points).
questions.final_answer: children become independent and live a better life.( – for 6 points)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Illustrate different types of programme planning in Early Childhood Education with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction: Programme planning in preschools means preparing and organizing activities for
  • children in a systematic way. It helps teachers ensure that children get opportunities for learning
  • play, creativity, and social development in a balanced manner((1 marks)).
  • Types: Long term(Yearly/Annual Plan), Short term(Monthly & Weekly Plan) and Daily
  • planning(Day-wise Plan) ((6 marks)- (2 marks) for explanation of each type). Suitable examples for
  • each ((3 marks)- (1 mark) for each)
questions.final_answer: each (- for each)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
